# Reconciliation (T-V3-1, lane V3)
`MpsCalc.Engine.Reconciliation.QuoteReconciler` recomputes the nine v13.4.1 measures from a quote's input and compares them with
what the calculator reported. It is **not wired into any endpoint, calculator or screen** (R-V3-1): it is a pure function a later
lane can call (a readiness panel, a pre-issue check, a test).
## What "independent" means
The module calls nothing in `QuoteCalculator` or `PurchaseCalculator` and shares no helper with them (a test scans the module's
source for that). Every figure is rebuilt from:
* the quote **input** (quantities, pages, flags, the line's declared pricing method, the term, the finance rate, the target GP,
the service costs, the supplies model), and
* the **facts the result records** for a line that come from a reference lookup the module cannot see: the tier-priced device and
option costs, the cost per page with the service reserve, the extended software prices, a purchase line's unit cost and applied
percent, a catalogue sell price.
A calculator bug that is consistent with itself (a line dropped from every total; a margin on price applied as a markup) is
invisible to the calculator's own parts-sum checks. It is visible here, because the module sums the lines itself and applies the
line's declared method itself.
`QuoteReconciler.ReconciliationTolerance = 0.01m`, **inclusive**: `|recomputed - reported| <= 0.01` passes (ruling D-13 a, "cents,
matching C-30"; v13's own are 0.015 and 0.02).
## The nine measures by quote mode
| Measure | Rental | Purchase |
| Upfront sell | not applicable (no upfront charge) | Σ section totals, each rounded to cents (X-21) |
| Upfront cost | not applicable | Σ unit cost × quantity, non-optional lines (X-07, X-10, X-19) |
| Upfront gross profit | not applicable | Σ (unit sell − unit cost) × quantity (X-05), before the partner rebate |
| Monthly revenue | Σ quantity × (base + pages × click + software), R-18 | the usage clicks over the monthly pages (X-16, X-26); only with a supplies model |
| Monthly cost | R-17 | the monthly pages × cost per page (X-14, X-16); only with a supplies model |
| Monthly gross profit | R-19 | revenue − cost; only with a supplies model |
| Annual gross profit | monthly GP × 12 | monthly GP × 12; only with a supplies model |
| Contract gross profit | contract value − monthly cost × term | upfront GP + monthly GP × term |
| Contract value | R-22 (annual step escalation) | upfront sell + monthly revenue × term |
A measure that does not apply is `NotApplicable` with a reason. It is never reported as a pass of zero. A quote the calculator did
not price has nothing to reconcile: all nine are `NotApplicable`.
Where the result carries no figure for a measure (annual gross profit; rental contract gross profit; the purchase monthly figures),
the **reported** side is the one the result's own totals imply (for example its monthly GP × 12, or its contract click revenue
÷ term). The rule text of each variance says which.
## What is not recomputed
* The partner rebate (X-11, X-12) is a payout, not a margin component: it is in none of the nine.
* The replacement shortfall of whole supply units (X-17, X-27) is an exposure at the end of the contract: it is in none of the nine.
* Fixed usage rates **without** a supplies model: the calculator prices no usage revenue or cost for them, so there is nothing to
* The rental result does not record a device's paper format (A3 or A4), which picks the service-cost column of the input. The
rental overload therefore also takes the `ReferenceData` and reads that one lookup from it.

### The Home list: staff-only columns and the Ready to Export group (B309 T-V0-8)
**Shape first, values later.** Lane V0 writes the contract; lane V2 (which owns `QuoteFigures.cs`) fills the values.
- **Four staff-only columns on a list row** (`GET /api/v1/quotes`): `oneOffGp`, `annualRecurringGp`, `tcv`, `totalGp` (exact decimal
strings, like every figure). A caller holding `internal-metrics` receives them; for anyone else the endpoint removes them from
every row (`Mapping.Restrict`), whatever the filling code produced. A quote with no calculation has none. Until lane V2 fills them
no row carries them. They are the only cost-side figures a list row may hold; every other member stays customer-safe (B46).
- **`group=readyToExport`** is a value of the list's `group` query parameter: *approved and not yet exported* (ruling C-23 MPS-3 (a)).
Until lane V2 adds it to `QuoteFigures.ListFilter.Parameters["group"]` the server answers it `400 INVALID_FILTER` like any value not
listed; the row's own `group` member keeps its four values (`drafts`, `submitted`, `rejected`, `approved`).
- **"Exported" means (the contract's definition):** the quote's current version has at least one `proposal-generated` event with
`isDraft` false, that is, a proposal was generated from its approved snapshot. No export flag exists; that event is the nearest
record (`QuoteEvents.ProposalGenerated`, written by `GET …/proposal`). So *ready to export* = current version Approved and no such event.
- **No CSV endpoint.** The Home CSV is built in the browser from the list rows it already holds (MPSCALC-245); the contract gains no route for it.
### Approve re-checks the submitted calculation (B309 T-V0-4, MPSCALC-234)
`POST …/approve` reads the submitted snapshot's calculation again, after the ownership, status and self-approval checks. If it is
`Blocked` or holds a `Blocking` issue the answer is **409 `BLOCKING_ISSUES`**, the code `POST …/submit` uses for the same condition,
no approved snapshot is written, no event is recorded, and the version stays Submitted (the approver rejects it with a reason). Through
the API this cannot happen to a version submitted by this server, because submit refuses it first; the check guards a snapshot stored
by other means, and `callerCan.approve` is false for it. An approvable version approves exactly as before.
### Audit of customer, reference, term and opportunity edits; "issued" and "accepted" (B309 T-V0-6, MPSCALC-236)
- **Old and new, without a reason.** A `PATCH …/draft` that changes `customer`, `quoteRef`, the term (`assumptions.termMonths`) or an
opportunity field (`accountManager`, `deliverySite`, `opportunityNotes`, `opportunityDeviceCount`) adds one audit entry per field to
the version's audit (the `priceAudit` list): `{ sequence, at, by, persona, field, oldValue, newValue, reason }`, an empty text counting
as no value. Unlike a purchase price they need **no reason** (the save still answers 200 without one); the save's `reason`, when
sent, is kept on the entries. A save that changes none of them, including an unchanged re-save (T-V0-3), records nothing. Creating
a quote records no such entry. Like the price audit, the list is returned to internal-metrics callers only and is frozen into
the snapshots (which restrict it the same way).
- **"Issued" is the `proposal-generated` event with `isDraft` false.** A proposal printed from an approved snapshot already
records that event (`GET …/proposal`, B35 item 5); a second kind for the same act would record it twice, so there is no `issued` event kind. The
*status* "Issued" ruled by D-12 a is a different thing and is a later change.
- **`accepted`** is now a kind in the contract's event list. **Nothing records it in this change**: the acceptance record (a reference
and a date on the Won outcome) is the held follow-up, which will write it. No quote has an `accepted` event yet.
### Version diff (B309 T-V0-5, MPSCALC-235)
`GET /api/v1/quotes/{quoteId}/versions/{n}/diff?against={m}` (Seller or Approver) answers what changed in version **n** compared with
version **m** of one quote: *old* is version m, *new* is version n. A version is read from its approved snapshot, else (while
Submitted) its submitted snapshot, else its draft and, if its latest calculation is for its current revision, that calculation;
`versionSource` and `againstSource` say which (`approved`, `submitted`, `draft`).
- `changes`: each draft field that differs, `{ path, oldValue, newValue }`, in path order. A list line is keyed by its own number or id
(`fleet[2].quantity`, `sections[office].markupPercent`, `hardware[1:OPT-TRAY].quantityPerDevice`), so an added line does not shift
the others; a missing side means the field was not there. A number written at another scale (3 and 3.00) is not a change.
- `figures`: each headline figure that moved, `{ name, oldValue, newValue }`: every decimal of the portfolio (`portfolio.monthlyCharge`,
`portfolio.contractValueExTax`, …) and of the purchase result (`purchase.…`) present on either side. Empty when a version has no calculation to read.
- **Internal-metrics.** A caller without it receives the same redacted drafts and restricted calculations the quote and snapshot reads
give them, so no cost, GP, margin, capital or target GP appears in `changes` or `figures`. A caller with it also gets those.
- **404 `NOT_FOUND`** for an unknown quote or an unknown version; **400 `BAD_REQUEST`** when `against` is missing, repeated, not a
version number (1 or more), equal to `n`, or when any other query parameter is sent. Administrator-only callers get 403 `FORBIDDEN`.
- A read: it stores nothing, records no event and changes no revision.

The draft (create, `PATCH …/draft`, every read and snapshot) carries four optional fields, left out on every quote stored before B309:
